items.passage: When Grant climbed the stairs to the roof, I was pinning wet towels to the line and kept pinning. He was my brother's tutor, and he had brought the school's accident form, already half filled in: slipped on the seawall, no one at fault. "It reads cleaner this way," he said. I took the pen and crossed out "slipped." My brother had jumped because I told him he couldn't, and I had laughed when he landed wrong. Grant watched me write that in the margin, slowly, in letters too large for the space. Later he warned that the principal would only ask more questions. "Then she can ask me," I said. Below us, a neighbor's rooster strutted along the fence, and the trade wind lifted the towels so they snapped like flags over the tin roofs.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show the narrator choosing to record her own part in an accident over a tidier account
To describe how the narrator's brother hurt himself on a seawall after accepting a dare
To illustrate how a tutor helps a family complete the paperwork a school requires
To suggest that people in authority always reward those who tell the truth
items.explanation: 화자는 Grant가 미리 채워 온 '미끄러짐, 아무 잘못 없음'이라는 문구에서 'slipped'를 지우고 자신이 동생을 부추겼다는 사실을 적는다. 뒤에서 교장이 더 물을 것이라는 경고에도 "Then she can ask me"라고 답해 자기 책임을 감수하는 태도가 다시 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 사고 일화만 요약했고, C는 서류라는 소재를 쓰지만 서술 목적이 다르다. D는 지문에 근거가 없는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Cape Town had turned cold for the funeral, and in their grandmother's yard the hives sat under sheets like furniture in a closed house. Harriet pressed a parcel into Rangi's hands before the mourners had finished their tea. Inside was a jar of honey with a hand-lettered label: Orange Blossom, Gran's last harvest. Rangi knew at once that it was not; the hives had been empty since winter, and the lid came from the supermarket. He held the jar to the window anyway and said the color was exactly right. Harriet smiled too widely and agreed. Later, when an aunt asked to taste it, Rangi said he was saving it, and Harriet looked at him with something close to gratitude. Along the fence, a row of agapanthus nodded blue heads against the wet brick.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Harriet gives Rangi a jar of honey at their grandmother's funeral gathering.
Two cousins quietly sustain a well-meant pretense for each other's sake.
The grandmother's beekeeping declined steadily during her final winter.
Grief makes every family gathering awkward for the people who attend.
items.explanation: Rangi는 꿀이 할머니의 마지막 수확이 아니라는 것을 알면서도 색이 딱 맞다며 맞장구친다. 뒤에서 이모가 맛보려 하자 아껴 두겠다고 막아 주고 Harriet이 고마워하는 듯 바라보므로, 두 사촌이 서로를 위해 선의의 연기를 함께 지켜 가는 것이 요지인 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 벌통 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 진술이다.

items.passage: Steam and the smell of frying garlic filled the galley where I mended the crew's uniforms while our ship sat in Shanghai for repairs. Meilin, my only apprentice, worked across the table on a torn cuff. That morning the cook, Burak, had burned his hand, and we had both seen it happen. By noon the captain wanted statements. Meilin said the pan had slipped; I had seen Burak reach for it without a cloth. We argued quietly, needles moving. I assumed she was protecting him. Then she described the angle of the handle and the jolt of the hull against the pier, details I had missed because I had been watching his face. We wrote two accounts and signed both. Outside the porthole, gulls fought over a crust on the black water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how a ship's cook burned his hand while the vessel was docked
To describe the daily routine of mending uniforms in a crowded ship's galley
To show the narrator realizing that a conflicting account reflected another view
To argue that witnesses should always trust their own eyes over others' words
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 Meilin이 Burak을 감싸려고 다르게 말한다고 여긴다. 그러나 Meilin이 손잡이 각도와 선체의 흔들림처럼 화자가 얼굴을 보느라 놓친 세부를 말하자 두 진술을 모두 서명해 제출하므로, 다른 진술이 거짓이 아니라 다른 시점에서 나왔음을 깨닫는 과정이 핵심인 C가 정답이다. A는 사고 일화만, B는 배경 소재만 말한다. D는 지문의 결론과 반대 방향의 일반론이다.

items.passage: Three rules governed my father's roadside diner outside Thessaloniki: coffee before questions, cash in the blue tin, and nobody touched the drawer under the register. My sister Themba and I had not spoken in four years when we met there to sell the place to Stavros, the cook who had worked beside our father for decades. While Stavros counted plates, Themba opened the forbidden drawer. Inside were her school report cards, every one, and a postcard I had sent from Lisbon, its corners soft from handling. We had each believed our father favored the other. Themba slid the postcard toward me without a word, and I pushed one of her report cards back toward her. Neither of us mentioned the sale again that afternoon. On the highway, a truck loaded with watermelons downshifted for the curve, its brakes sighing.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To list the rules that the narrator's father relied on to run his diner
To recount how two sisters arrived at a diner to sell it to its longtime cook
To suggest that family secrets are always better left undiscovered
To show how a hidden discovery unsettles the sisters' belief about their father
items.explanation: 서랍 속에는 Themba의 성적표와 화자가 보낸 엽서가 함께 닳도록 보관되어 있었고, 자매는 각자 아버지가 상대를 편애했다고 믿어 왔다. 이후 두 사람이 말없이 물건을 서로에게 밀어 주고 매각 이야기를 꺼내지 않는 대비가 그 믿음이 흔들렸음을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 도입의 소재만, B는 일화만 말하며, C는 지나치게 일반적이고 지문과 맞지 않는 교훈이다.

items.passage: Lucius found his son already in the backyard vineyard the morning after the storm, kneeling where the wind had torn out the oldest vine behind their South Side two-flat. Its roots had pulled up a rusted lunchbox. "Leave it," Lucius said, but the boy had already pried it open. Inside lay a photograph of Lucius at nineteen, grinning on a club stage with a trumpet, and a ticket stub from Forty-Seventh Street. For years Lucius had told his son, who practiced guitar behind a closed door, that music was no way to feed a family. The boy looked at the photograph a long time, then set it on the fence post and began pressing soil back around the roots. Next door, Beulah called over to ask whether the grapes had survived, and Lucius said most of them had.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Lucius most likely tell his son to "Leave it"?
options: He does not want his son to find evidence of a past that contradicts his warnings.
He worries that the oldest vine will die if its roots are disturbed any further.
He wants his son to replant the vine before Beulah notices the storm damage.
He suspects the rusted lunchbox belonged to an earlier owner of the two-flat.
items.explanation: 상자 안에는 열아홉 살의 Lucius가 트럼펫을 들고 무대에 선 사진이 있었다. 바로 이어 그가 수년간 아들에게 음악으로는 가족을 먹여 살릴 수 없다고 말해 왔다는 문장이 나오므로, 두 문장을 이어 읽으면 자신의 말과 모순되는 과거를 들키고 싶지 않았다는 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 없는 다른 걱정, C는 이후 행동을 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Nobody had expected Kenji to come. The fishing season had been the worst in twenty years, and in October he had told Sakura he would leave her boat for a factory job in Sapporo. Yet here he stood at the back of the crowded wedding hall in a borrowed suit, holding a gift wrapped in newspaper. Sakura, who had taught him to mend nets since he was fifteen, watched him search the crowd until he found her nephew, the groom. Kenji had once told her that the boy was the only one in the harbor who never laughed at his clumsy knots. He handed over the parcel, bowed deeply, and slipped out before the speeches. Snow had begun falling on the parking lot, softening the outlines of the delivery vans.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Kenji most likely attend the wedding?
options: He hopes to persuade Sakura to let him return to work on her boat.
He wants to honor the groom, who was kind to him when others mocked him.
He needs to deliver a gift on behalf of his new factory in Sapporo.
He wishes to apologize to the harbor for the season's poor catch.
items.explanation: Kenji는 식장에서 신랑을 찾아 선물을 건넨 뒤 곧바로 떠난다. 바로 다음 문장에서 그가 신랑을 항구에서 유일하게 자신의 서툰 매듭을 비웃지 않은 사람이라고 말했다는 단서가 나오므로, 그 친절에 대한 감사를 표하러 왔다는 B가 정답이다. A는 배와 관련된 다른 바람, C는 지문에 없는 외부 이유, D는 흉어기라는 소재를 엉뚱하게 동기로 바꾼 선택지다.

items.passage: Kerala's monsoon was drumming on the tin roof of the school music room when Arjun found me there, tuning the harmonium I had sold him a year before. I run the instrument shop by the bus stand, and the school calls me for repairs. All that spring Arjun had come into my shop each week, insisting that the harmonium's flat reed had cost his daughter her place in the state competition. Every time, I had refused to admit fault. That afternoon he did not mention the competition. Instead he pointed to Theo, a boy who would compete next month on an instrument no better than his daughter's, and asked whether I could teach him to hear a reed going flat before a judge did. I said yes before I had decided to. Rain kept pooling under the door, and the caretaker laid sacks across the threshold.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Arjun most likely ask the narrator to help Theo?
options: He wants to force the narrator to finally admit that the harmonium was at fault.
He hopes to earn a refund for his daughter by bringing the shop a new customer.
He wants to keep another young player from losing to a flaw no one noticed.
He has been asked by the school to find a qualified music teacher for Theo.
items.explanation: Arjun은 음이 낮아진 리드 때문에 딸이 대회에서 떨어졌다고 믿어 왔다. 이어서 Theo가 딸의 것만큼 나쁜 악기로 다음 달 대회에 나간다는 점과 심사위원보다 먼저 리드 문제를 듣게 가르쳐 달라는 부탁이 나오므로, 두 단서를 이어 보면 같은 일이 다른 아이에게 반복되지 않게 하려는 C가 정답이다. A는 그가 과거에 품었던 다른 감정, B는 지문에 없는 이익, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: By six the bus to the hills was already late, and Dolores stood under the shelter with a cement-gray handprint still on her shirt. That morning, in front of the whole crew, she had backed the mixer into the site office and knocked the foreman's lunch off the windowsill. Armand had stared at the spilled rice for a long moment. Now he arrived at the stop, set down his bag, and offered her half of a roti he had bought to replace it. "Office needed a new door anyway," he said. She laughed, then covered her mouth, still half ashamed, and he laughed louder so that she would not have to stop. Below them the lights of Port of Spain came on in loose strings, and a dog trotted past with great purpose.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Anxious and embarrassed, dwelling mainly on the young worker's mistake
Mostly embarrassed, with only a passing hint of the foreman's kindness
Nostalgic, recalling the city's evenings from a great distance in time
Warmly humorous, with traces of lingering embarrassment
items.explanation: 지문에는 Dolores가 동료들 앞에서 실수한 일과 여전히 반쯤 부끄러워 입을 가리는 모습이 있지만, 더 두드러지는 것은 Armand가 로티를 나눠 주며 농담하고 그녀가 웃음을 멈추지 않도록 더 크게 웃어 주는 따뜻한 유머다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서인 당혹감만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었다. C의 향수는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Mumbai was still gray when Tara let herself into her uncle's bakery through the back door, the ovens ticking as they warmed. Coach Riccardo was already there, as he was every Saturday, buying pav for the team. He did not look up from the trays. So the rumor had reached him: that she had called his lineup a joke in front of the selectors. She had said the words, though not about him. Tara tied on an apron and began dusting loaves, flour rising in small clouds, and the silence stretched until her hands ached from working. At last Riccardo asked whether the cardamom buns were fresh. She said they would be in ten minutes. He said he would wait. Outside, a delivery boy leaned his bicycle against the shutter and counted coins into his palm.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
options: Tense and uneasy, though softened by a tentative hint of reconciliation
Quietly hopeful, as two old friends look forward to a warm reunion
Mostly at ease, though briefly interrupted by a flicker of strain
Festive and bustling, in keeping with a busy morning at a city bakery
items.explanation: Riccardo가 고개를 들지 않고 침묵이 손이 아플 만큼 길게 이어지는 장면은 긴장과 불편함을 주된 분위기로 만든다. 그러나 그가 빵이 신선한지 묻고 기다리겠다고 말하는 부분에서 화해의 조심스러운 기미가 비치므로 A가 정답이다. B는 덜 두드러진 희망만 말했고, C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, D의 떠들썩함은 지문에 단서가 거의 없다.

items.passage: After the third morning of rain, Dayoung stopped pretending he came only for mackerel. He stood in the doorway of the rented farmhouse on Jeju while Shuang wrapped the fish in newspaper, and he asked, too quickly, how the old man still knotted the straw ropes that held the thatch down against the wind. Shuang said nobody wanted to learn that anymore. Then he handed Dayoung the end of a rope and, without looking at him, corrected the boy's grip twice, his thumb pressing the strands into place. When Dayoung finally tied a knot that held, Shuang tugged it once, nodded, and grumbled that the fish would spoil if the boy kept him talking. Beyond the stone wall, the wind combed the barley flat and let it rise again.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Dayoung and Shuang?
options: Dayoung is eager to learn, but Shuang has no interest in teaching him anything.
Shuang is a gruff but willing teacher to a boy eager to learn a fading craft.
Shuang depends on Dayoung to keep the farmhouse's thatched roof in repair.
Dayoung is a regular customer who thinks of Shuang only as a fish seller.
items.explanation: Shuang은 아무도 배우려 하지 않는다고 퉁명스럽게 말하지만 곧 밧줄 끝을 건네며 소년의 손을 두 번 고쳐 잡아 준다. 매듭이 성공하자 한 번 당겨 보고 고개를 끄덕이면서도 투덜대는 모습을 이어 읽으면, 무뚝뚝하지만 기꺼이 가르치는 관계임을 알 수 있어 B가 정답이다. A는 Dayoung 쪽 감정만 반영했고, C는 도움의 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 손님과 상인이라는 통념에 기댄 선택지다.

items.passage: Because a flooded road was holding up the buses, Niamh and Rory were the only two left in the camp dining hall in Galway, each at the far end of a long table. They had not spoken all week. Rory broke the silence by saying that a counselor had told him he played the fiddle "like someone apologizing." Niamh laughed, then stopped, and admitted that a teacher had once said the same about her singing, years ago, and she had not sung since. Rory slid his fiddle case down the table toward her. "Then you can sing badly while I play badly," he said, and she moved three seats closer. Rain streamed down the tall windows, and somewhere in the kitchen someone was stacking trays one at a time.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Niamh and Rory?
options: Rory pities Niamh, who resents him for prying into her painful past.
Niamh offers to coach Rory, who is anxious about his fiddle playing.
Two near-strangers discover a shared hurt and begin to encourage each other.
Longtime camp rivals compete over which of them has more musical talent.
items.explanation: Rory가 상담사에게 들은 말을 털어놓자 Niamh도 선생님에게 같은 말을 듣고 노래를 그만두었다고 고백한다. 이어 Rory가 바이올린 케이스를 밀어 주며 함께 서툴게 해 보자고 하고 Niamh가 세 자리 다가앉으므로, 같은 상처를 확인한 두 사람이 서로를 격려하기 시작하는 관계인 C가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만 지어냈고, B는 격려의 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 없는 경쟁 관계라는 통념이다.

items.passage: Folasade read the last of their mother's letters aloud while Obinna sat by the guesthouse window, where the monks' bell rope hung motionless in the noon heat of Dakar. The plan had succeeded: the house in Lagos was sold, the debts were paid, and their mother would join them before the rains. Every letter said she was grateful. Not one said she was glad. Between the final pages Folasade found a pressed hibiscus, faded to the color of weak tea, which their mother had always picked from the vine beside the old front door. Obinna turned it over in his palm and remarked that the new house had no such vine. "We can plant one," Folasade said. He laid the flower on the windowsill, and neither of them moved to return it to the envelope, though the breeze kept nudging it toward the edge.
items.question: In the text, the pressed hibiscus most likely represents
options: the debts that the sale of the house in Lagos has finally settled.
the quiet routine of the monks that the siblings hope to imitate.
the new house that the mother will soon share with her children.
the attachment to home that the mother gave up for the siblings' plan.
items.explanation: 히비스커스는 어머니가 옛집 현관 옆 덩굴에서 늘 따던 꽃이고, 편지에는 고맙다는 말만 있을 뿐 기쁘다는 말은 없다. Obinna가 새집에는 그런 덩굴이 없다고 말하는 대목까지 이어 보면, 이 꽃은 계획을 위해 어머니가 포기한 집에 대한 애착을 나타내므로 D가 정답이다. A는 매각의 결과, B는 배경 소재, C는 꽃과 반대되는 새집을 가리켜 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Astrid did not believe in new gates. For forty years she had repaired the oak gate of the cemetery in Bergen, replacing one rotten slat at a time, so that by now hardly a board of the original remained. Her apprentice, Anahera, wanted to mark the gate's hundredth year with something grand: a carved arch, the town's name in gold leaf. Astrid only handed her a plane and a single slat cut from the same stand of oak. "One board," she said. "Each year, one board." Anahera fitted it beside a slat that Astrid's own teacher had set, and the grain of the two ran nearly together. That evening the gate swung shut behind the last mourners, and the hinges, oiled that morning, made no sound at all.
items.question: In the text, the cemetery gate most likely symbolizes
options: a tradition kept alive through small renewals passed between generations.
the private grief of the mourners who visit the cemetery every evening.
Anahera's desire to bring bold and visible changes to the old town.
the gradual decline of careful craftsmanship in a modernizing city.
items.explanation: 문은 한 번에 한 장씩 판자를 갈아 원래 판자가 거의 남지 않았지만 여전히 같은 문으로 서 있다. Astrid는 화려한 기념물 대신 해마다 한 장씩이라는 방식을 전하고, Anahera의 판자가 Astrid의 스승이 끼운 판자 옆에 결이 이어지듯 놓이므로 문은 세대를 거쳐 조금씩 새로워지며 이어지는 전통을 상징한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 근거가 약하고, C는 Astrid가 받아들이지 않은 Anahera의 처음 계획일 뿐이다.

items.passage: Istanbul spread below our hillside terrace like a dropped tray of glasses, all glitter and edges, and my brother and I sat above it with a ledger neither of us wanted to open. Our lamp shop had sold four lamps in a month. Makana, a buyer from Honolulu who had wandered up the wrong steps, asked to see the back room. There, under dust sheets, were our grandfather's brass lanterns, the ones we had stopped displaying because they seemed old-fashioned. Makana lifted one to the window and turned it slowly, and the pierced brass threw stars across the walls. __Our cramped little shop, which had seemed to us a sinking boat, became in his hands a lit harbor.__ My brother set the ledger down. On the next roof, a woman was shaking out a red carpet, and the dust drifted off over the water.
items.question: The underlined sentence in the text primarily serves to convey that
options: the shop is physically located near the water at the bottom of the hill.
the brothers fear that Makana will carry their lanterns away overseas.
Makana's interest recasts a business that seemed doomed as one with promise.
the grandfather's lanterns are too delicate to be used outdoors at night.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 가라앉는 배처럼 보이던 가게가 Makana의 손에서 불 밝힌 항구가 되었다는 은유다. 앞에서 한 달에 램프 네 개밖에 팔지 못했다는 실패 상황과, 형제가 숨겨 둔 할아버지의 등을 Makana가 빛에 비춰 보는 장면을 이어 보면 방문자의 관심이 가게의 가능성을 드러냈다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 은유를 문자 그대로 읽었고, B와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: On the first mild evening of April, Captain Vesna walked out to the parish garden behind the harbor chapel in Riga, where the widows grew their cabbages in long and obedient rows. Tatiana, the girl who had hidden in her hold all the way from Danzig, was kneeling among them, pulling weeds she could not name. Through the whole voyage she had refused to speak of her family or her home. Now she asked, without looking up, what the captain's ship had been called before it was renamed. "It bore my mother's name," said Vesna, "and no one has spoken it in twenty years." She spoke it then, softly, into the cooling air. __The word sat between them like a lantern set down upon a dark road, and for a while neither wished to walk past it.__ At length Tatiana began to speak of the village she had fled, and the captain did not interrupt her.
items.question: The underlined simile in the text most strongly suggests that the spoken name
options: made both women uneasy, as though it warned of danger on the road ahead.
reminded the captain chiefly of the long and difficult voyage from Danzig.
was too painful for either woman to bear hearing a second time.
offered a shared warmth that both women wished to linger beside.
items.explanation: 밑줄 직유는 이십 년 만에 입 밖에 낸 이름을 어두운 길에 내려놓은 등불에 비유하고, 두 사람 모두 그것을 지나쳐 가고 싶어 하지 않았다고 말한다. 이후 말이 없던 Tatiana가 처음으로 고향 이야기를 꺼내므로, 그 이름이 두 사람 사이에 머물고 싶은 따뜻한 빛이 되었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 등불을 위험 신호로 잘못 읽었고, B와 C는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Three rules for the orchard, Sadia wrote on the board:
no climbing, no picking, finish what you start.
Jordan kept the first two and broke the third,
his survey of the old guava trees half-drawn.
Now, each Thursday, they walk the rows in silence,
teacher and student, a gap the width of a fence.
__His clipboard is a closed door under his arm.__
Sadia counts the trunks aloud for both of them;
he marks them down and does not answer.
At the far wall of the Karachi orchard, one tree still holds
a single green fruit it has not dropped.
Wind moves through the dry canals toward the sea.
items.question: The underlined metaphor in the text most nearly suggests that
options: Jordan uses the unfinished project to keep Sadia from reaching him.
Jordan has finally completed his survey and wants to keep it private.
the clipboard is too heavy for Jordan to carry through the orchard.
Sadia has shut Jordan out of the classroom until his work is done.
items.explanation: 밑줄 은유는 Jordan의 클립보드를 팔 아래 끼운 닫힌 문에 비유한다. 앞에서 그가 끝마치지 못한 조사 때문에 둘이 울타리 너비만큼 떨어져 말없이 걷는다고 했고, 뒤에서 Sadia가 대신 수를 세어도 그는 대답하지 않으므로 미완성 과제가 교사를 막는 벽이 되었다는 A가 정답이다. B는 조사가 반쯤 그려져 있다는 사실과 맞지 않고, C는 은유를 문자 그대로 읽었으며, D는 문을 닫은 주체를 뒤집었다.

items.passage: Caoimhe was already at the bus depot in Chiang Mai when I arrived, sitting on her suitcase among the songthaews and the smell of diesel and grilled pork. Twenty years ago we had shared a stage in Dublin, two voices in one act, until she left to nurse her father and I, Elisa, took the tour on alone. For years I told myself the account was settled, that she had made her own choice. Then she laughed at something the ticket clerk said, and I heard it again: the low harmony I had built a whole career trying to replace. __Her laugh was a key I had pocketed and never returned.__ We bought two tickets to Pai. She let me carry the heavier bag, and I did not argue.
items.question: The underlined sentence in the text primarily conveys that the narrator
options: has lost her ability to sing well since the two women parted ways.
realizes she kept something of Caoimhe's that she never repaid.
recalls only happy memories of the years the two women toured together.
believes Caoimhe is still angry that she took the tour on alone.
items.explanation: 밑줄 은유는 Caoimhe의 웃음을 화자가 주머니에 넣고 돌려주지 않은 열쇠에 비유한다. 앞에서 Caoimhe가 아버지를 돌보러 떠난 사이 화자가 홀로 투어를 이어 갔고, 그녀의 화음을 대신하려고 경력을 쌓았다고 말하므로, 화자가 상대의 것을 가져가고 갚지 않았음을 깨닫는다는 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 지문에 근거가 없고, D는 화자의 죄책감을 상대의 분노로 바꾼 선택지다.

items.passage: I kept the secret for a whole monsoon. I was Xinyi, the ferryman's daughter, eleven years old, and after classes the gymnasium of my school in Colombo became my hiding place. Faisal, a regular passenger on my father's boat, found me there one afternoon among the stacked mats. He knew, as I did, that my father had run the ferry in weather the harbor office had forbidden, and that a fine would ruin us. He asked only whether I was all right. __My silence was a held breath, and I had grown dizzy keeping it.__ He nodded as if I had answered, and from then on he never spoke of that crossing to anyone. The basketballs in the corner cage smelled of rubber and old rain.
items.question: The underlined sentence in the text most strongly suggests that
options: the narrator felt physically ill from the humid air inside the gymnasium.
the narrator longed to shout the secret to everyone in her school.
keeping the secret had become an exhausting effort for the narrator.
the narrator was holding her breath so that Faisal would not find her.
items.explanation: 밑줄 은유는 화자의 침묵을 참고 있는 숨에 비유하고, 그것을 지키느라 어지러워졌다고 말한다. 화자가 장마철 내내 비밀을 지키며 체육관에 숨어 지냈다는 앞부분과 이어 보면, 침묵을 유지하는 일이 점점 견디기 힘든 부담이 되었다는 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었고, B는 지문에 드러나지 않은 충동이다.

items.passage: Navajo country stretches flat and red from the roof of our house, where the water tank stands like a patient animal. My mother, Ayita, and I climbed up to check the level before the wedding, because two hundred guests would need washing water and coffee. She had the guest list open on her phone, and halfway down it was my father's name. "He'll come if you ask him," she said, rapping the tank and listening for the hollow note. We had planned the food, the music, and the blankets, but we had not __settled__ whether I could forgive him enough to send the invitation. I watched her tap the metal again, lower this time, where the sound went solid. Far off, a pickup crawled along the highway, raising a thread of dust.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "settled" most nearly mean?
options: Sunk
Calmed
Paid
Decided
items.explanation: 밑줄 단어 앞에서 화자와 어머니는 음식, 음악, 담요는 모두 계획했다고 말한다. 그러나 아버지를 용서하고 초대장을 보낼지는 아직 정하지 못했다는 대비이므로 'settled'는 '결정하다'라는 뜻이고 D가 정답이다. A는 물탱크 침전물에서 연상되는 뜻, B는 감정을 가라앉힌다는 뜻, C는 빚을 청산한다는 뜻으로 이 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Rehearsals were never easy. Each evening Aung walked his stepdaughter, Amelia, to the old stone bridge over the Pasig, where the noise of the river covered her mistakes and she could practice her recital piece without the neighbors listening. He knew nothing of the violin and did not pretend to. Yet over that hot month in Manila he had learned to __mark__ the places where she faltered: a pause in the third phrase, a slur that came apart. He never mentioned them; he only lingered a little longer over those passages when he hummed the tune on the walk home, so that she heard them again without being told. Neither of them guessed that Amelia, years later, would call these walks her truest lessons. Below the bridge the barges slid past, heavy with rice, their lanterns swinging.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "mark" most nearly mean?
options: Notice
Label
Grade
Celebrate
items.explanation: Aung은 바이올린을 전혀 모르지만 Amelia가 머뭇거리는 곳을 알아차리게 되었고, 그것을 말하지 않고 콧노래로 그 부분을 더 오래 불러 줄 뿐이다. 따라서 'mark'는 표시를 남기거나 점수를 매기는 것이 아니라 '알아차리다'라는 뜻이므로 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 겉으로 표시하거나 평가한다는 뜻인데, 그가 실수를 한 번도 언급하지 않았다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D도 문맥과 무관하다.
